chunks: Do you not see that the boundaries of your cities have diminished, your populated areas have been conquered, your possessions have been snatched away and your cities and lands have been attacked.
May Allāh have mercy on you, get up to fight your enemy and do not remain confined to the earth, otherwise you will face oppression and suffer ignominy and your fate will be the worst.
The warrior should be wakeful because if he sleeps the enemy does not sleep; and that is an end to the matter.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of vigilance in warfare according to Malik al-Ashtar's letter?
ai.summary: In this urgent dispatch to Malik al-Ashtar, Imam Ali (AS) employs a rhetorical question to highlight the rapid erosion of Egyptian territories, framing military vigilance as a divine imperative to prevent permanent humiliation. The famous maxim 'the brother of war is wakefulness' underscores the Shia strategic principle that peace is maintained through constant readiness, a concept deeply rooted in the concept of *Jihad al-Nafs* and *Jihad al-Talal* in governance. This passage reflects the practical application of Imam Ali’s justice, linking territorial defense directly to the preservation of the community's dignity and faith.
